title: panic_if
concept: panic_if is a concise way to express 'if this condition is true, panic with this message' — combining the check and the abort in one line.
why: Repeated 'if x { panic(...) }' patterns are verbose. panic_if makes guard conditions more readable and signals intent clearly.
tips: Use panic_if for production guard clauses — it's always active, unlike assert
Chain panic_if calls at the start of functions — fail fast before any work is done
Keep the message actionable — tell the caller what went wrong AND what's expected
panic_if reads naturally: 'panic if this condition is true' — self-documenting
common_mistakes: Using panic_if for input validation that should return Result — prefer recoverable errors when possible
Writing panic_if with inverted logic — remember it panics when the condition IS true
Overusing panic_if for minor issues — reserve it for truly unrecoverable situations
